sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned AC to SC 11.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioners no. 8, 11, 14 and 15 were deleted from the array of parties as petitioners vide order dated 06.11.2023, as such, relief in the instant writ application is confined to rest of the petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3. It is next contended by the learned counsel that on the raiyaiti land of the petitioners as detailed at para 5 of the writ petition at village Baigani, Block Hulasganj, District Jehanabad a water conservation project was constructed without acquiring the land by the respondents, as such, no compensation was paid.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4. It is next submitted that petitioners were paying rent of the land up-till 2011 as would manifest from Annexure-2 to the writ application.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is further submitted that petitioners are small farmers and they do not have any other land, except the one as detailed at para 5 of the writ application which has been acquired forcefully by brute police force without compensating the petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the petitioner no. 2 and 11 filed C.W.J.C. Patna High Court CWJC No.4014 of 2020(22)
dt.11-11-2024 No. 19729 of 2010 which was disposed of by an order dated 22.04.2014 (Annexure-3 to the writ application) with a direction to the Collector to dispose of the matter within three months, as the matter was pending consideration before the Collector, Jehanabad.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 5. It is submitted that in compliance of the order dated 22.04.2014 passed in C.W.J.C. No. 19729 of 2010, the Collector carried out a threadbare investigation and passed a detailed order dated 28.08.2015 (Annexure-4 to the writ application) for payment of compensation to the petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel submits that the Collector in his order dated 28.08.2015 recorded that the S.D.O., Jehanabad vide his letter dated 01.07.2014 intimated that on account of drying up of river jalwar about 60-70 years back, the State Government about 25-30 years back had settled the land pertaining to jalwar river with the petitioners and others.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The petitioners are paying rent, further land relating to Khata No. 148, Plot No. 755 area 20.25 decimals at village Baigani was settled by the S.D.O. in favour of Lalan Paswan, Arjun Mochi and Suresh Paswan vide Parwana dated 28.11.1985.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Further, at times, compensation has been sought by the land holders when their crops got destroyed when the river was in spate.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Further, the Circle Officer vide his letter no. 487 dated 30.06.2014 had intimated that lands as detailed in C.W.J.C. No. 19729 of 2010 pertaining to Khata No. 148, Patna High Court CWJC No.4014 of 2020(22) dt.11-11-2024 Khesra No. 755, area 12.41 acres pertaining to Thana No. 690, Mauja Baigani is recorded as Gair Majarua Malik, Kism Zamin, river jalwar in survey Khatiyan.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Further, the Circle Officer also recorded that vide Settlement Case No. 03/85-86 same land was settled with three petitioners of C.W.J.C. No. 19729 of 2010 (petitioners no. 8 herein who stands deleted was also a petitioner in C.W.J.C. No. 19729 of 2010, hence, the Circle Officer recorded that lands were settled with three petitioners of C.W.J.C. No. 19729 of 2010), further rent has also been paid by Lalan Paswan and Suresh Paswan with regard to Jamabandi No. 2008-09 and 1990-91, but no Jamabandi was created with regard to Arjun Mochi, son of Kalicharan Mochi, the Circle Officer also intimated that the lands apart from being settled with the aforesaid persons was also settled with 19 other persons vide Settlement Case No. 03/85-86 and Settlement Case No.
80/95-96, as would manifest from Jamabandi created, thus from the letter dated 30.06.2024 of the Circle Officer, it manifests that the land was settled with 22 persons.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. Further, the S.D.O. in his letter dated 01.07.2014 placing reliance on letter no. 1226 dated 08.05.1981 issued by the Revenue and Land Reforms Department, Government of Bihar has recorded that the letter dated 08.05.1981 confers power on the S.D.O. to settle lands in rural areas for the purposes of housing and Patna High Court CWJC No.4014 of 2020(22) dt.11-11-2024 agriculture with SC/ST/OBC (Schedule-1), further Gair Majarua Aam Land are to be settled by the State Government.

entities.text: Revenue and Land Reforms Department, Government of Bihar
entities.label: ORG

sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. Further, Executive Engineer, Water Resources Sub- Division (Water Wage Division), Jehanabad vide his letter no. 533 dated 02.04.2014 had intimated that due to drying up of river jalwar, the villagers were using the land of the river for agriculture when Bihar Irrigation Act, 1997 incorporates that land pertaining to river bed, is under the Water Resources Department and the land cannot be settled without seeking permission of the Water Resources Department.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Further, the Executive Engineer in support of his contention relied on notification dated 25.04.2003 which was issued in terms of the Bihar Irrigation Act, 1997.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Collector recorded that the notification relied by the Executive Engineer issued in terms of the Bihar Irrigation Act, 1997 was issued 11 years after the land was settled.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Thereafter, the Executive Engineer vide his letter no. 1126 dated 08.08.2014 produced the survey map of 1913-14 in which Khesra No. 755 has been shown as river jalwar,
thereafter the Collector held a meeting with the Executive Engineer and asked him to produce any circular based on which it can be held that earlier settlements were illegal based on which the Executive Engineer submitted Bihar Irrigation Act, 1997, accordingly, a legal opinion was sought from the Government Advocate, Jehanabad who opined that the S.D.O. had Patna High Court CWJC No.4014 of 2020(22) dt.11-11-2024 the power of settling the land, hence, the land settled by the S.D.O. was in accordance with law.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Further, from perusal of the Bihar Irrigation Act, 1997, it manifests that the same incorporates that land pertaining to river bed cannot be settled without the permission of the Water Resources Department but then the Bihar Irrigation Act, 1997 came into force after the settlements were made and the 1997 Act is not retrospective in operation.
sentences._hearing_file: Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024.json

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the Patna High Court CWJC No.4014 of 2020(22) dt.11-11-2024 Collector after considering the report of the C.O., S.D.O. and the issues put forth by the Water Resources Department came to a considered conclusion that petitioners of C.W.J.C. No. 19729 of 2010 are entitled for compensation and thus directed the Land Acquisition Officer to send his report to the Executive Engineer in terms of the report of the Circle Officer after measurement of the land and the Executive Engineer was directed to seek funds from the Water Resources Department for paying the compensation.
11.
22. Learned counsel next submits that opinion of the learned Advocate General records that though compensation cannot be given to the petitioners in terms of the RTFCTLARR Act, 2013 on the ground that there is no provision in the Land Acquisition Act for giving compensation with regard to the land emerging from the river and after the opinion of the learned Advocate General, the entire gamut of the case changed and the compensation of Rs.4 crores and odd as asked by the District Land Acquisition Officer from the Water Resources Department was turned down.
It is submitted that if the lands which the Collector, Jehanabad now is claiming to settle with the petitioners is the same land which was settled with the petitioners about more than 50 years back,
the same amply demonstrates that the land is not land emerging from the river but is Gair Majaura Malik Land and in support of the said contention, the learned counsel for the petitioners relies on the revisional survey wherein the land had been recorded as Gair Majaura Malik Land.
Nand Lal Das vs The State Of Bihar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138576831/
6 25.
It is submitted that it has been wrongly pleaded that land has been marked out by the authorities for settling with the petitioners when there is no land on the spot vacant for being settled.
